instruction: Convert form.docx on the desktop to a PDF document and save it in the forms folder of my Google Drive.

args.query: title = 'form.pdf' or title = 'form.docx' or title = 'form.docx.pdf' or title = 'forms'

metadata.explanation: Simplified instruction. Evaluator checks PDF exists in forms folder with 1 page.

llm_judge_reasons: Page count hardcoded to 1 without verifying the actual page count of source form.docx - if source has multiple pages, evaluator will incorrectly fail
No content verification: evaluator cannot verify that the PDF actually contains the converted content from form.docx (any 1-page PDF >10KB would pass)
File pattern matching is limited to 'form.pdf' and 'form.docx.pdf' - would miss valid alternatives like 'form (1).pdf' if user saves with different name
No verification that form.docx existed on desktop initially - cannot verify the 'conversion' aspect, only that a PDF exists in the folder
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add metadata analysis to determine actual page count of form.docx from the source file, then use that as ref_value instead of hardcoded 1
Consider using a getter to check form.docx page count or add it to config metadata with evidence
Use broader file pattern matching (e.g., regex pattern 'form.*\.pdf$') or check for any PDF in forms folder created after task start
For full verification: compare PDF text content against expected content from form.docx, or at minimum verify PDF file size matches expected range based on source document
